events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Holmes City
events.description: 1 death. Douglas County. A tree fell on a camper, and unfortunately one of the two individuals inside the camper was killed. The other individual was injured and hospitalized.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Blomkest
events.description: 1 death. Kandiyohi County. A grain bin blew over and landed on a man who was about to enter a vehicle. This resulted in a fatality.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near (otg)worthington Arp
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Nobles County. Several power poles were snapped by strong thunderstorm winds, which downed powerlines across Interstate 90. A car stopped on the roadway to avoid crossing downed powerlines, and was struck from behind by a tractor trailer, resulting in the (indirect) fatality of one vehicle passenger and injury of the other three passengers in the car as well as one from another car.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Rochester
events.description: 1 death. Olmsted County. One person was killed east of Rochester when a 40 foot pine tree was snapped off, fell and landed on the individual and his pickup truck.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Mankato
events.description: 1 death. Blue Earth County. A tree branch fell onto a tent at the Land of Memories Park. A family was in the tent and a 4 year old girl was killed from injuries of the fallen tree branch.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Crane Lake
events.description: 1 death (indirect). St. Louis County. On the morning of July 19, 2021, between 10 and 10:30am CDT, a line of sub-severe thunderstorms caused a canoe with two occupants to capsize. Neither were wearing life jackets and one of the two occupants drowned. The incident occurred on Loon Lake east of Crane Lake, Minnesota, within the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness (BWCAW). Estimated wind speeds along the line of storms were 25-30 mph based on nearby observations.

events.title: Tornado near Dalton
events.description: 1 death. Otter Tail County. This tornado began in Grant County, but after about two miles, it crossed into Otter Tail County, where it ended about 5 miles east of Dalton. The total track through both counties was about 9 miles. Peak winds were estimated at 170 mph, based on available damage indicators. At least 10 farmsteads were impacted, with three homes, one pole shed, and one machine shed destroyed.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Mc Comber
events.description: 1 death (indirect). St. Louis County. Marginally severe storms moved through the area during the early afternoon hours leading to sporadic downed trees. Following the storms, a homeowner was on his roof removing a downed tree when he lost his footing and fell approximately 20 feet to the ground and landing on a propane tank. First responders attempted life saving efforts upon arrival, but the homeowner died on the scene. The closest observing site to the location of the fatality was the Ely Airport which reported a max gust to 30 mph during the storm, but higher gusts were likely based on the tree damage reports.

events.title: Flood near Redwood Falls
events.description: 1 death. Redwood County. The local police department reported that an individual had disappeared in the Redwood River near the 100 block of West Bridge Street and was presumed dead from drowning.

events.title: Flood near Franklin
events.description: 1 death. Renville County. Flood waters slowly receded from excessive rainfall that occurred Tuesday morning. Numerous roads were impacted by the flood waters, especially south of Highway 212. An individual was found in a water-swollen drainage ditch, two days after his car was discovered submerged a mile upstream.

events.title: Heavy Rain near Mc Gregor
events.description: 2 deaths (indirect). Aitkin County. Two individuals were killed with three others injured, one with life-threatening injuries, when one vehicle skidded into another. Pavement was wet from recent rainfall. According to the MN State Patrol, all involved in the crash were wearing seat belts.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Forest Center
events.description: 2 deaths. Lake County. Severe thunderstorm winds knocked down numerous trees near the Prairie Portage area of Basswood Lake right on and near the Canadian border. Trees were blown down near the campsite of 9 campers who were affiliated with the Boy Scouts of America. One woman (age 39) and one boy (age 13) were killed when trees fell on their tent. Two other campers were injured with non-life-threatening injuries. The campers were technically in Canada, but added this to the event record for historical purposes since the campers were so close to the US border.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Marais
events.description: 1 death. Cook County. A large tree trunk was snapped several feet above ground level and the tree landed on a man and his son who were camping on Duncan Lake. The tree killed the father, Craig Walz, the brother of Minnesota Representative Tim Walz, as well as seriously injuring Craig's son. The son was airlifted to a hospital in Duluth.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Red Wing
events.description: 1 death. Goodhue County. Numerous trees were blown down between Red Wing and Wacouta. An individual was injured during this storm from a fallen tree that landed on a detached garage, and trapped him as the garage collapsed.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Green Isle
events.description: 1 death. Sibley County. Several media outlets and local officials indicated that an individual died from a fallen tree north of Arlington near Highway 15. The individual was on a four-wheeler in the pasture of his farm and attempted to herd his cattle to safety during a storm. Thatï¿½ï¿½ï¿½s when a tree fell on him, officials indicated.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Goodview
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Winona County. The driver of a pickup truck was killed in Goodview when sub-severe thunderstorms winds uprooted a tree from the side of a bluff. The tree fell into the roadway and landed on the truck the man was driving.
